nodes.label: Body measurements
nodes.detail: Bust, waist, hip and back length set the block, available intake and starting side lengths. Body remains fixed in step 4.

nodes.label: Waist ease
nodes.detail: Adds to full waist circumference. Changes waist widths, available intake and side shaping.

nodes.label: Hip ease
nodes.detail: Adds to full hip circumference. Changes hip widths and hip-to-waist takeout.

nodes.label: Waist-to-hem length
nodes.detail: Moves the hem level and changes lower seam slopes and lengths. Must exceed hip depth.

nodes.label: Hem fullness
nodes.detail: Total horizontal addition, not curved hem length. Each side edge receives F × share / 2; each princess edge F × share / 4.

nodes.label: Fullness distribution
nodes.detail: Four nonnegative shares sum to one. Redistributing a share requires compensating changes elsewhere. It does not change total F.

nodes.label: Widths & intake
nodes.detail: D = hip + hip ease − waist − waist ease. Back takeout = (D − 1) / 4; front = (D + 1) / 4. Both must be positive. The engine splits each reduction between princess intake and side shaping.

nodes.label: Lower panel geometry
nodes.detail: Waist, hip and hem endpoints determine lower curves. Length, fullness and distribution interact: equal fullness does not imply equal flare angle or seam length.

nodes.label: Side balance & transfer
nodes.detail: Side-dart intake is the unrotated front side length minus the back side length. If it exceeds 0.08 cm, the upper side front rotates around BP. This creates an indirect path from lower design changes to upper geometry.

nodes.label: Resolved panels & marks
nodes.detail: The engine rebuilds seams, princess controls and corresponding height-derived notch locations. Changes in curves can alter paired interval lengths even when total lengths are close.

nodes.label: Cutting outlines
nodes.detail: The fixed allowance is applied to changed stitch contours. Concave regions and strong flare can challenge offset validity. Outline tests assess sampled geometry and containment.

nodes.label: Geometry validity
nodes.detail: Finite inputs, positive takeout, valid stitch/cut polygons, notch consistency and engine parity are engineering conditions. Existing parameter caps are implementation guards, not proven safe ranges.

nodes.label: Design intent
nodes.detail: Straightness, taper and flare limits must be defined before a range can be called suitable for an intended style. A straight side seam is not automatically the largest wearable waist ease.

nodes.label: Seam compatibility
nodes.detail: Measure each interval between paired marks, as well as totals. The 0.1 cm flag is diagnostic. Unknown intended ease remains unknown, including below the flag threshold.

nodes.label: Physical wearability
nodes.detail: Fabric, movement, closure and a measured wearer or form provide evidence unavailable from flat geometry. No current map edge establishes wearable limits.
